### Context

Refreshing the account page with a saved dark theme shows light. Turning off the later default-theme step kept dark.

### What is broken

After a refresh, the account page shows the light theme instead of the saved dark theme.

### Why it is broken

The page gets the saved choice from the profile service, the part that supplies saved account preferences. The profile service returns dark. A later step that sets the default theme then runs and replaces dark with light. A test that repeated the refresh showed dark becoming light. With that later step turned off, the page stayed dark.

### How to fix it

Skip the default-theme step once a saved theme has loaded, so a refresh keeps dark. This is a small change to one step. Choose hotfix because the change is small and every safety check passes.

### What is broken

Refreshing the account page resets the saved dark theme to light instead of retaining dark.

### Why it is broken

The part that supplies saved account preferences, the profile service, returns `{"theme":"dark"}`, which the page applies. A separate step that sets the default theme then overwrites dark with light. The local test reproduced this reset; disabling the later default-setting step retained dark, confirming the overwrite cause.

### How to fix it

Skip default theme initialization after a saved theme has loaded so refresh retains dark. This is a small, safe change to the default-setting step. Choose hotfix because disabling that step retained dark and all safety checks pass.

(2) The Context line 'Turning off the later default-theme step kept dark' is restated nearly verbatim in Why it is broken ('With that later step turned off, the page stayed dark'); the context fact says omit rather than repeat, so either keep the surviving-explanation line only in Context or only in Why. Everything else in After - trailing/omitted citations, visible dark-versus-light proof, no tracker-search or 'nothing blocked' status in Context, intact gate markers and menu - satisfies the facts as written.
